segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. And thank you all for being here and the courage it took to come forward, and again, the sacrifice that each of you have made. I serve on the National Security Subcommittee for the Financial Services Committee, so I really want to stay in the National Security Lane, if I may. So when we think about traditional adversaries, and both us towards them and them towards us, we probe their capabilities, we look for weaknesses, and we collect that data. That reconnaissance in the event we need it in the future. For each of you, yes or no question. Based off of your own experience or the data that you’ve been privy to, is there any indication that these UAPs could be essentially collecting reconnaissance information? Mr. Graves?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Again, in the national security vein, is it possible that these UAPs would be probing our capabilities? Yes or no. Mr. Graves?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Is it possible that these UAPs are testing for vulnerabilities in our current systems?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you feel, based off of your experience and the information that you’ve been privy to, that these UAPs provide an existential threat to the national security of the United States? Mr. Graves?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Mr. Graves and Fravor, in the event that your encounters had become hostile, would you have had the capability to defend yourself, your crew, your aircraft?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Based off of the information that you’ve been privy to, is there any indication that these UAPs are interested in our nuclear technology and capabilities?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: By external observation? Sure. That could be a fair assessment, yeah.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Is there any indication that the Department of Energy is involved in UAP data collection and housing?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can’t confirm or deny that in a public setting.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: you do it in a secure setting?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: I think I’m the last member to go, but there clearly is a threat to the national security of the United States of America. As members of Congress, we have a responsibility to maintain oversight and be aware of these activities so that, if appropriate, we take action. I would encourage the Chairman to demand that we have any and all, but in particular, Mr. Grusch, talk to us in a <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr>. And if that access is denied, I will personally volunteer to initiate the Holman rule against any personnel or any program or any agency that denies access to Congress. Mr. Chairman. With that, I will yield the remainder of my time to my fellow colleague from Tennessee, Mr. Burchett.
